defs.def: either of the organs on the sides of the head that you hear with 耳；耳朵

ex.s: I woke up early and rushed out of the door in my eagerness to get to know my new school.
ex.t: 我很早就醒了，急切地冲出门去了解我的新学校。

ex.s: I woke up really early and tip-toed to the kitchen.
ex.t: 我真的很早就醒了，踮着脚走到厨房。

ex.s: May I come and get it early tomorrow morning?
ex.t: 我可以明天一大早来取吗？

ex.s: The noise from the LRAD is directed like a ray of light and travels only into the ears of that person, but it is not deadly.
ex.t: LRAD发出的噪音像一束光线一样定向传播，只进入那个人的耳朵，但它不会致命。

ex.s: A couple of years ago, film-maker David Bond realised that his children, then aged five and three, were attached to screens to the point where he was able to say "chocolate" into his three-year-old son’s ear without getting a response.
ex.t: 影片制作人大卫·邦德(David Bond)在几年前意识到，他的孩子当时五岁三岁，被贴在屏幕上，以至于他可以在三岁的儿子的耳朵里说"巧克力"而没有得到回应。

ex.s: My parents urged me to get out of this so-called unhealthy habit, but their repeated requests fell on deaf ears.
ex.t: 父母劝我改掉这个所谓不健康的习惯，但他们的一再要求都被我当成了耳旁风。

ex.s: He believes bus drivers are the eyes and ears of students when they're away from home and they have a gift to discern what kids are feeling.
ex.t: 他认为，当学生们离家在外时，公交车司机就是他们的眼睛和耳朵，并且他们有一种辨别孩子们感受的天赋。

defs.def: having the type of ears mentioned 构成形容词
an ability to recognize and copy sounds well 灵敏的听力；辨音力
the top part of a grain plant, such as wheat, that contains the seeds （谷类植物的）穗
